independent_computation.claim_under_test_A: New value asserts: 'Every declared family on this item is a defence.'

declared_families_on_3157: damage (resistance-mitigation, related to damage-instance, armor-penetration, magic-penetration)
test_A.result: FALSE. Two of the four cached atoms are not defensive: stats.ability-power (105 AP is a pure offence stat) and the atom filed under family "damage". The cached family vocabulary contains no "defence" family at all, so the universal-quantifier claim cannot be satisfied by the data as cached.

independent_computation.claim_under_test_B: New value asserts: 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.'

test_B_offence_from_stats.step_2: Syndra Q (Dark Sphere) AP ratio = 70% AP (data/champions.json).
test_B_offence_from_stats.step_3: Delta raw magic damage per Q cast from this item = 0.70 * 105 = 73.5.
test_B_offence_from_stats.step_4: Post-mitigation against an illustrative 60 MR target: 73.5 * 100 / (100 + 60) = 45.94 per Q cast.
test_B_offence_from_stats.result: The item measurably increases outgoing damage. Its represented mechanics are not durability-only.

test_B_offence_from_the_active_itself.step_1: Time Stop's own wiki text says the wielder is 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items' for 2.5 s.
test_B_offence_from_the_active_itself.step_2: docs/math-foundations.md §1.1 models autos as N(T) = floor(AS * u * T) and casts as occupancy on one shared timeline. A 2.5 s stasis window inside the fight window is 2.5 s of zero attack rate and zero cast occupancy.
test_B_offence_from_the_active_itself.step_3: Autos forgone at Syndra's level-1 base attack speed alone: floor(0.658 * 2.5) = 1 swing, rising with bonus AS; casts forgone: Q's 7 s base cooldown means a 2.5 s freeze displaces up to a full Q cast (>= 90 + 0.70*AP raw) out of any window it straddles.
test_B_offence_from_the_active_itself.result: Stasis strictly REDUCES outgoing TDD over the window it occupies. It is precisely a mechanic that changes outgoing TDD, which is the opposite of what the new string asserts.

independent_computation.claim_under_test_C: Old value asserts: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input; item presence alone never assumes stasis.'

test_C.step_1: Time Stop is an ACTIVE (data/items.json places it under "active", not "passives"), so it only takes effect when the player chooses to use it.
test_C.step_2: Because using it costs 2.5 s of the shared cast/auto timeline (test_B above), assuming stasis from item presence would silently subtract damage that a scenario never asked for; assuming no stasis while pricing it would silently add damage. The only sound treatment is to price it from an explicit, bounded active-seconds input.
test_C.step_3: The wiki text also fixes the bound the input must respect: 2.5 seconds per use.
test_C.result: TRUE and consistent with both the cached wiki text and the timeline model in docs/math-foundations.md.

conclusion: The old value is a correct, sourced statement about Zhonya's Hourglass; the new value is contradicted twice by the cached data: (1) the item declares stats.ability-power (105 AP), an offence family, so 'every declared family is a defence' is false, and the cached vocabulary has no 'defence' family; (2) Time Stop's own wiki text (2.5 s unable to attack or cast) plus the shared-timeline model in docs/math-foundations.md make stasis a mechanic that lowers outgoing TDD, not a durability-only mechanic. The rewrite replaces a true, item-specific rationale with a false generalisation.
caveat: The scenario definition for 'syndra_custom_order_39' is not present in the exported data/ tree (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains 22 scenarios, none Syndra), and src/, tests/ and scripts/ were out of scope, so the item at item_coverage[1] was identified from the leaf's own old text ('Time Stop') rather than from the scenario build list. If the change also reordered item_coverage so that index 1 now names a different item, this verdict applies to the Zhonya's Hourglass rationale as quoted.
